advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the git-dir pointer resolution in _resolve_common_git_dir so an OSError reading .git yields None (unlocked) instead of propagating, matching the 'best-effort throughout' contract.
evidence: _resolve_tracker_git_dir at gitutil.py:74-76: 'if os.path.isfile(tracker_git):\n        with open(tracker_git, encoding="utf-8") as f:\n            gitdir = f.read().strip()' — no try/except; a TOCTOU unlink or permission error raises OSError

fetch_coordination_lock docstring: 'Best-effort throughout: if the common dir cannot be resolved (not a git repo), the lock file cannot be opened, or a wedged peer holds it ... the block proceeds UNLOCKED'
The lock body only guards os.open (gitutil.py:~466 try/except OSError) and the commondir read (gitutil.py:419), not the git-dir pointer read reached before them.
advisory.finding: fetch_coordination_lock is documented as 'best-effort throughout' (proceed unlocked when the common dir cannot be resolved), but _resolve_common_git_dir -> _resolve_tracker_git_dir reads the .git pointer file with a bare open() and no OSError guard, so an unreadable or concurrently-unlinked .git file raises OSError out of the context manager rather than yielding unlocked, turning a fetch-coordination best-effort path into a hard failure.
scenarios: A linked worktree's .git file is momentarily unreadable (permission or concurrent worktree prune/relocation) while a fetch is starting.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _resolve_common_git_dir, wrap the _resolve_tracker_git_dir call in try/except OSError returning None (or add the guard inside _resolve_tracker_git_dir), so any filesystem read error resolves to the unlocked best-effort path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply _jitter to the CAS-mismatch retry backoff in both fetch paths, consistent with the module's existing jittered backoff policy.
evidence: git_fetch.py:388-389 'if cas:\n            time.sleep(_CAS_RETRY_BACKOFF_S)' — fixed delay, no jitter
gitutil._jitter docstring: 'so competing processes de-synchronize instead of thundering in lockstep (9305 research rec #4)'
advisory.finding: The CAS-mismatch retry backoff is a fixed, un-jittered sleep in both the snapshot path (_CAS_RETRY_BACKOFF_S) and the sync path (_FETCH_CAS_BACKOFF_S), so when several non-rebar git peers contend on the shared remote-tracking ref they can re-collide in lockstep on each bounded attempt, defeating the retry's purpose; the rest of this module deliberately jitters its backoff (_jitter, git lockfile.c shape).
scenarios: Two or more non-rebar git peers repeatedly racing the same refs/remotes/origin/tickets CAS while a rebar fetch retries.
